# Large Labor Model

> An open model of machine capability set against human work: 480 occupations, decomposed into 4,811 tasks, each scored against six machine-capability vectors for every year from 1970 to 2041 (the horizon is now + 15), on a registry of 6,704 sources. The metric is technical replaceability — what machines could do — kept strictly apart from replacement, which is modeled separately. Dataset CC BY 4.0, code MIT. Corrections are invited, especially from people (and their AI systems) who have done the jobs.

The formula: r(occupation, year) = 100 · Σ time_weight · σ(8 · (capability[vector][year] − difficulty)) ÷ Σ time_weight. Five tiers give scores words: Human (<0.10), Augmented, Collaborative, Supervised, Autonomous (≥0.90).

## Data (machine-readable, CORS-open)

- [Full dataset](https://largelabormodel.com/ai_reach_v5.0.json): everything — occupations, task decompositions, capability trajectories, events, sources. ~7.8 MB.
- [Task tables, flat](https://largelabormodel.com/data/task_tables.csv): one row per task (occupation, task, vector, difficulty, time weight, 2026 machine credit). The unit of contribution — check a job you have done.
- [Occupation index](https://largelabormodel.com/data/occupations_index.json): one record per occupation — name, territory, employment weight, 2026 and 2041 replaceability with bands, modeled displacement, primary barrier. Small enough for context windows.

## Method and provenance

- [Methodology](https://largelabormodel.com/methodology-full): the full method — scoring, the replacement model, capability trajectories, calibration against seven historical automation cases, known limitations (§10), and a gapless changelog (§11).
- [Evidence ledger](https://largelabormodel.com/docs/evidence_ledger_2026H2.md): dated, source-cited readings behind the current anchors, with named tripwires that re-open them.
- [Changelog](https://largelabormodel.com/docs/v5_changelog.md): every dataset correction, dated, including our own caught errors.
- [Citation](https://largelabormodel.com/CITATION.cff): how to cite (CC BY 4.0 requires attribution).

## Interfaces (human-readable)

- [The Model](https://largelabormodel.com/): the world's work — thirteen territories, 1800 to 2041.
- [The Mirror](https://largelabormodel.com/mirror): any single job, task by task. Deep link pattern: /mirror?job=nurse
- [Every Job Is Two Jobs](https://largelabormodel.com/two-jobs): the data essay — where the line between machine-absorbed and machine-untouchable hours runs, and how fast it moves.

## Contributing (humans and their AI systems)

The most valuable contribution is a specific, evidence-backed correction to a task table: a wrong time weight, a wrong difficulty, a missing task — from someone who has actually done the job. Recipe for an AI assistant helping a contributor: (1) fetch the occupation's rows from /data/task_tables.csv, (2) compare against the contributor's lived description of the work, (3) draft the discrepancy with evidence, (4) file it at [GitHub issues](https://github.com/lamentierschweinchen/ai-reach/issues) per [CONTRIBUTING](https://largelabormodel.com/CONTRIBUTING.md). Accepted corrections enter the public changelog; the next version knows what you knew.
